correctness.rationale: Finite-dimensional polar rank criterion is reconstructed: active edge differences have rank 10 minus the number of connected components, giving exactly all facet normals. Tight spanning trees imply integral potentials, and diameter two implies a complete search over 59049 ternary words. The packaged verifier executed successfully, independently enumerating binary and three-level candidates, checking 17 disjoint signed-S5 orbits and a fixed-point Burnside sum. A separate clique bound proves 20 maximum tight edges and equality precisely at twelve complementary Hamiltonian decompositions.

originality.rationale: The general tight-edge facet criterion is prior work (arXiv:1910.05193, Theorem 3.1). The explicit 1032/17 complete T5 symmetry classification, five incidence multiplicities and independent 20/12 Hamiltonian equality theorem were not identified in the inspected sources, own accessible previous claims, or searched graph/polytope records. Published J(n,2) projection constants concern another Banach invariant, and published Petersen graph facets concern the complementary graph rather than the line graph. value.rationale: Complete natural finite metric Banach-space facet classification, not just an incidental count: 17 complete S5×sign orbits with representatives, incidence spectrum over five classes and two height levels, plus structural 20-vertex maximum and 12 Hamiltonian equality cases proved independently of enumeration. The triangular graph is the canonical line graph of K5 and complements the Petersen graph, motivating the exact benchmark without inventing downstream consequences.
